lead.description: Fisher's cup experiment for testing a claim to tell whether milk or tea was poured first

self_checks.title: Number of divisions
self_checks.prompt: Eight cups are divided into two labelled sets of four. How many divisions are there, and what is the null probability of the correct one?
self_checks.answer: There are 70 divisions. The null probability of the correct one is 1/70.

self_checks.title: Three correct
self_checks.prompt: In the eight-cup design, how many sets get exactly three of one kind right, and what is the null probability of a score at least that good?
self_checks.answer: There are 16 such sets. Including the one perfect set gives 17/70.

self_checks.title: Six cups
self_checks.prompt: Six cups, three of each kind, must be split by naming a set of three. What is the null probability of a perfect score?
self_checks.answer: There are 20 divisions, so the probability is 1/20 = 0.05.

overview_sentence: The [Lady tasting tea](articles/lady-tasting-tea.qmd) is Fisher's experiment for testing a claim to tell whether milk or tea was poured first.
